title: The Bench Standard for Grading a Returned Item — Northbeam Returns and Restocking
content:
Every item returned on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking authorisation is inspected before the refund is worked out, and the inspection is completed within the schedule's inspection days counted in business days from the day the item was booked in. The grade recorded by the inspection governs what is refunded, and the customer's account of the condition does not stand in for it. An item is graded as new and sealed only where the packaging has not been opened; an opened item with everything in the box is graded open box complete, and one missing anything is graded open box incomplete with the schedule's deduction taken for each missing accessory. Damage the customer caused is graded as such, damage or failure present on arrival is graded defective on arrival, and an item that cannot be put right economically is graded beyond economic repair. Where the schedule requires the original packaging and it is missing, the item is graded open box incomplete rather than refused, and the deduction applies. Where the serial returned does not match the serial sold the item is not graded at all: the return is refused and the item is sent back to the customer at the retailer's cost.

## The grading standard, condition by condition

| What the bench finds | The grade recorded |
| --- | --- |
| the packaging has not been opened | as new and sealed |
| opened, everything that belongs in the box is there | open box complete |
| opened, something is missing from the box | open box incomplete, with the schedule's deduction for each missing accessory |
| damage the customer caused | damaged by the customer |
| damage or failure present on arrival | defective on arrival |
| cannot be put right economically | beyond economic repair |
| the original packaging is missing where the schedule requires it | open box incomplete, and the deduction applies |
| the serial returned does not match the serial sold | no grade at all: the return is refused and the item is sent back to the customer at the retailer's cost |

## Where the authority sits

The grade that governs what is refunded is the grade the inspection recorded on the authorisation, read from the return authorisation record for that order line together with the serial it carries. The customer's account of the condition does not stand in for it. The grade is in place before the refund is worked out.

## Questions the standard answers

**May an item be graded as new and sealed where the customer says the carton was never opened but the bench found the seal broken?** No. The grade rests on what the inspection recorded, and the packaging having been opened puts the item on the open box grades.

**Is a missing carton a ground for refusing the return on a schedule that requires the original packaging?** No. The item is graded open box incomplete instead, and the schedule's deduction for each missing accessory applies.

**What does a serial that does not match produce?** Not a grade and not a deduction. The return is refused, and the item goes back to the customer at the retailer's cost.

**How long may the bench take?** The schedule's inspection days, counted in business days from the day the item was booked in.
